name: Saint Peter Claver
history: A Catalan Jesuit who spent nearly forty years at Cartagena, in present-day Colombia, the chief slave port of Spanish America. He met each ship as it came in, going down into the holds with food, water and medicine, nursing the sick and teaching and baptising the enslaved. He called himself the slave of the Africans for ever.
life: Peter Claver was born at Verdú in Catalonia in 1580 and joined the Jesuits in 1602. At the college in Majorca the elderly porter, Saint Alphonsus Rodríguez, urged him to go to the Americas. He reached Cartagena in 1610, was ordained there in 1616, and signed his final vows as Peter Claver, slave of the Africans for ever. Thousands of captives arrived in the port each year, chained and starving after weeks at sea. Claver went aboard with interpreters, carried food and medicines, washed wounds and stayed with the dying. He taught the faith with pictures, baptised, by tradition, some three hundred thousand people, and visited the sick in the hospitals and the prisoners of the city. Struck by illness in 1650, he spent his last years largely forgotten in his room. He died on 8 September 1654, and Leo XIII canonised him in 1888, together with Alphonsus.
prayerTo: Saint Peter Claver, you went down into the darkness of the slave ships to bring bread, medicine and the love of Christ. Pray for all who are trafficked, exploited or held in forced labour today, and for me, that I may not look away from suffering but go out to meet it with practical love. Amen.
penance: Give to a charity that works against human trafficking, or find out where the things you buy are made and by whom.
meditation: Claver taught that we must speak first with our hands and only then with our lips. What practical help could you give before you offer advice?
